title: Convolutional Neural Networks
learning_outcomes: Explain convolutional neural networks and accurately refer to at least two syllabus subtopics.
Apply the main idea of convolutional neural networks to a small example, trace, calculation, or scenario.
Identify one important assumption or failure mode and describe how to check it.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study convolutional neural networks in the context of deep learning. You will connect the PDF subtopics to a small example and practice describing what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Convolutional Neural Networks matters because it affects how data is collected, represented, analyzed, interpreted, or used in a decision. Check the task and assumptions before choosing a method.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Deep learning composes parameterized transformations and learns them using objective functions and optimization. Reliable results require appropriate data, validation, compute, and monitoring.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Keep the question, data grain, units, and assumptions explicit. If a result differs, inspect the input and steps in order. Avoid turning an observed association into a causal claim, treating a sample as the population, or assuming a small demonstration guarantees production behavior. Look at training and validation trends together; a single point is not a diagnosis.

hints: Write down the input, expected result, units, and assumptions first.
Change only one condition when testing a revised example.
Ask whether the data and method represent the real decision; do not infer causality or production readiness from a toy example.
